title: Review: IE evidence for sub-shells (period 3 dips); Mass spectrometry of elements; The mole and Avogadro constant; Empirical and molecular formulae; Concentration and standard solutions; Molar gas volume and Avogadro's law; Ideal gas equation and gas laws; Titrations and solution calculations; Limiting reagent and yield
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AM01#t2 term and clue written for the game; AM01#t3 term and clue written for the game; AM03#t1 term and clue written for the game; AM08#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM01#N.8a, AM02#N.7a, AM03#N.9, AM04#N.15a, AM05#N.4, AM08#N.9, AS02#N.8, AS06#N.6, AM01#N.9, AM02#N.11, AM03#N.11, AM05#N.7c.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Amount of substance
items.clue: The quantity with symbol n, found by dividing a mass by M.

items.label: Avogadro constant
items.clue: Multiply n by this value to get the number of particles, N.

items.label: Concentration
items.clue: Amount of solute divided by the volume of the whole solution.

items.label: Conical flask
items.clue: Vessel in which the two solutions meet, swirled over a white tile.

questions.stem: How many ions are there in 5.55 g of calcium chloride, CaCl₂? (N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹; Ar: Cl 35.5, Ca 40.1)
A hydrocarbon contains 88.80% carbon and 11.20% hydrogen by mass. Its Mr is 54.0. What is its molecular formula? (Ar: H 1.0, C 12.0)
A student adds 600.0 cm³ of water to 200.0 cm³ of 0.500 mol dm⁻³ NaCl(aq), giving 800.0 cm³ of solution. What is the concentration of NaCl in the diluted solution, in mol dm⁻³?
A sealed aerosol can is left in a car on a sunny day. At 20 °C the gas inside is at 3.00 × 10⁵ Pa. The can warms to 70 °C; its volume stays constant. What happens to the pressure inside the can?

options.text: It rises to 3.5 times its starting value.
It stays the same, because the volume is fixed.

questions.stem: Sulfur dioxide reacts with oxygen: 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2SO₃(g). What volume of oxygen reacts completely with 30.0 cm³ of sulfur dioxide? All volumes are measured at the same temperature and pressure.
questions.explanation: Same T and p, so volumes are in the coefficient ratio: 30.0 × 1/2 = 15.0 cm³.

questions.stem: A student records these titres: 24.30 cm³ (rough), 23.85 cm³, 23.40 cm³ and 23.50 cm³. Which mean titre should be used in the calculation?
questions.explanation: Only 23.40 and 23.50 cm³ are concordant (within 0.10 cm³). Their mean is 23.45 cm³.

questions.stem: Bromine atoms are about 50% ⁷⁹Br and 50% ⁸¹Br. Which describes the Br₂⁺ molecular-ion peaks in the mass spectrum of bromine?

options.text: m/z 158 and 162 only, in the ratio 1 : 1

questions.explanation: ½ × ½ = ¼ for 158 and for 162; 2 × ½ × ½ = ½ for 160. Ratio 1 : 2 : 1.

questions.stem: The first ionisation energies of phosphorus and sulfur are 1012 kJ mol⁻¹ and 1000 kJ mol⁻¹. Which explanation of the lower value for sulfur is correct?

options.text: Sulfur's outer electrons are shielded by more inner electrons than phosphorus's.
Sulfur's electron is removed from a sub-shell of higher energy than phosphorus's.
Sulfur loses an electron from a doubly occupied 3p orbital, where repulsion raises its energy.
Sulfur atoms are larger than phosphorus atoms, so their outer electron is further away.

questions.explanation: P has three unpaired 3p electrons; in S one 3p orbital holds a pair. Repulsion between them means slightly less energy is needed.

questions.stem: A one-carat diamond is pure carbon with a mass of 0.200 g. About how many carbon atoms does it contain? Data: Ar C 12.0; N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.
questions.explanation: n = 0.200 g ÷ the molar mass of C = 0.0167 mol. N = 0.0167 mol × N_A = 1.00 × 10²² atoms.

questions.stem: Ethyne, a welding gas, and benzene, a liquid, both contain 92.3% carbon and 7.7% hydrogen by mass. What is the molecular formula of benzene? Data: Ar H 1.0, C 12.0. Mr of benzene = 78.0.
questions.explanation: C: 92.3 ÷ 12 ≈ 7.7; H: 7.7 ÷ 1 ≈ 7.7. Ratio 1 : 1, empirical formula CH (about 13). x = 78 ÷ 13 = 6: C₆H₆.

questions.stem: Seawater contains about 1.29 g of magnesium ions, Mg²⁺, per dm³. How many moles of Mg²⁺ are in 250 cm³ of seawater? Data: Ar Mg 24.3.

Magnesium reacts with excess dilute hydrochloric acid: Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl₂(aq) + H₂(g). What volume of hydrogen, in cm³ at 298 K and 1 atm, forms from 0.120 g of magnesium? (Ar: Mg 24.3; molar gas volume 24.5 dm³ mol⁻¹ at 298 K and 1 atm)
